title: Balance Point? Centre of Mass Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A waiter holds a tray on one hand, a tightrope walker grips a long pole, a crane lifts a load by one hook. Each one finds a special point where all the mass seems to sit. And when Diya stacks four coins on one end of her ruler, the middle no longer balances. Where does it balance now, and why? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the centre of mass.

On a live motion notebook, a light rod carries two balls. As ball two gets heavier, the centre of mass slides toward it, the readout tracks X, r1 and r2, and a graph shows X climbing toward ball two but never passing it. We freeze at 1 kg and 3 kg to see m1 r1 = m2 r2, then double both masses to see that only the ratio matters. We build the formula step by step (mass-weighted average, units, the midpoint for equal masses, closer to the heavier mass, many particles in x and y), see link by link why the balance point is the centre of mass, compare equal and unequal balls side by side, and find the centre of three masses on a grid. Then the exam trap (the centre is not always halfway), an original JEE Main pattern question on a shifting particle, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
